problem: Modular frontier-based ObjectNav methods (SemExp, PONI, PEANUT) learn target-object relations only implicitly from distance-based supervision, while pure LLM approaches (L3MVN, LFG) decide from the current observation and fail when little semantic information is visible. Neither exploits explicit room-level common sense (a bed is in a bedroom) together with learned layout priors.
motivation: Efficiency (SPL) of ObjectNav lags far behind SR, because agents waste time exploring rooms unrelated to the target. Humans use object-to-room common sense, which an LLM can supply offline, and injecting it into supervised training could make the agent efficient while staying robust to wrong LLM knowledge.
key_idea: Query GPT-4 offline with chain-of-thought positive and negative prompts for object-to-room likelihoods, inject them into room-segmented floor maps as a third supervised frontier-scoring task (O2R potential) on top of PONI's object and area potentials, and train a multimodal multi-channel Swin-Unet with three decoders.
insight: The biggest gain comes from swapping the UNet for the multimodal Swin-Unet (73.6 to 75.2 SR, 41 to 42.1 SPL), and the LLM O2R decoder is the strongest single decoder, ahead of area and object potentials. Positive and negative prompts combined beat either alone (SPL 44.1 vs 43.0/43.8), while CoT adds little because it is applied only once offline. Gains are largest on room-specific objects (bed, toilet) rather than ubiquitous ones (chair).
method: LLM O2R knowledge: GPT-4 with CoT positive and negative prompts scores each room-object pair, h(r,o)=LLM_pos-LLM_neg in [-1,1], for Gibson and MP3D categories, computed offline once

O2R dataset: room-segmented 2D floor maps built from Gibson and MP3D mesh annotations; the LLM score is assigned per room and object channel, and frontier GT maps (object, area, O2R) are generated PONI-style from randomly augmented partial maps (800k train samples)

Multimodal input: 17-channel semantic map (explored, obstacle, 15 objects) with channel-wise PE, plus CLIP embeddings of top-3 room estimates, LLM target rooms and target category, and MLP-embedded distance and direction to the nearest object of each class, with a modal-type embedding
Multi-channel Swin-Unet: Swin-B encoder with separable-conv patch embedding and three Swin decoders predicting object, area and O2R potential maps, with skip connections
Uncertainty-weighted loss: photometric and SSIM losses for each of the three tasks fused with learnable aleatoric-uncertainty weights instead of fixed weights
Inference: fused frontier maps pick the highest-value frontier as the long-term goal, then FMM local planning; the long-term goal is re-selected every T=25 steps in the real world

setting.backbone: Swin-B multi-channel Swin-Unet with 3 decoders (trained), plus frozen CLIP ViT-B/32; GPT-4 used offline for knowledge; Mask R-CNN (Gibson) / RedNet (MP3D) for segmentation
setting.training_data: Generated frontier-map samples from Gibson Tiny (25 train scenes) and MP3D (61 train scenes), 800k training and 2k validation samples with augmentation; O2R scores from GPT-4
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + pose, projected to a top-down semantic map
setting.action_space: low-level move_forward / turn_left / turn_right / stop, with long-term goal frontier selection and FMM planner
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT segmentation only in an ablation; real-world pose from Hector SLAM LiDAR)

numbers.extra: Gibson Tiny 5 validation scenes, 200 episodes per scene, 500 step limit
numbers.evidence: Table ObjectNav validation results on Gibson and MP3D: Gibson SR 78.3, SPL 44.6
Table ObjectNav validation results: MP3D SR 50.1, SPL 19.1

numbers_note: Split is labelled 'validation' in the paper; recorded as 'val'. Real-world house results (SR 82.8, SPL 74.9, 30 episodes) are in a custom setting and not listed as a benchmark entry. Backbone size ablation is on Gibson.
results: LROGNav reaches Gibson SR 78.3 / SPL 44.6 and MP3D SR 50.1 / SPL 19.1, improving SPL by an average of 10.6% over the second-best methods (SemExp 41.0 on Gibson, PEANUT 16.3 on MP3D). RIM has slightly higher MP3D SR (50.3). In a real 50 m² house with a Kobuki robot, the average SR was 82.8% and SPL 74.9%.
limitations: Real-world tests are small (30 episodes in one Japanese-style house), with failures from collisions in narrow spaces and detection/depth errors; long-term goal interval T=25 differs from simulation
O2R knowledge is generated once offline and is static; CoT gives little gain, and the LLM knowledge is home-specific and does not generalize to other environments
Relies on noise-free pose in simulation and on segmentation quality (large gap with GT segmentation), and on the SemExp-style mapping module
